title: How a tiny static Fortnite countdown site earned $10,870 in passive revenue
summary: Priyam Raj built a single-page Fortnite season countdown to solve his own problem, and it grew into a near-zero-cost passive income stream. He layered on Epic's Support-a-Creator code, AdSense (unlocked by adding a blog) and an API to remove maintenance, reaching $10,870 lifetime revenue.

principles.text: Build a tiny tool that solves your own problem; it can find an audience on its own.
principles.quote: I just uh didn't want to keep the game open just to see how much time there was left for the next season

principles.text: Static sites host free, so costs stay near zero and revenue is almost pure profit.
principles.quote: the only cost that I was paying for this website each month was the um charge for the domain which I still am paying it's like 10 dollars a year on cloudflare

principles.text: Seed distribution by posting in the community where your audience already hangs out.
principles.quote: I posted about it on Reddit first and the site just started getting a lot of visitors

principles.text: Stack multiple monetization sources on the same traffic, like creator codes and ads.
principles.quote: I thought why not just promote my code on the website and then people would use it and let's see how much money can I make uh just with this website

principles.text: Automate the recurring manual work with an API so the site becomes truly passive.
principles.quote: I used that calendar API and integrated it to my website and now I never had to like uh update the code ever again

principles.text: Ad approval needs real content; adding a blog turned a thin one-pager into an AdSense-eligible site.
principles.quote: I was obviously rejected for having no content on the website and so I thought like uh should I just add a Blog to this thing and then try reapplying
